summary: Sprint-simulation scenario: 12-session sprint with requirement change for long-horizon coordination testing
context: Micro-task scenarios (2-5 agents, 5-15 min) don't test Twining's persistence advantage over long time horizons. Real teams accumulate decisions over weeks with requirement changes mid-sprint.
rationale: 12 sessions from 3 engineer personas with heterogeneous tasks (features, bugs, refactoring) and a mid-sprint requirement change (session 8: SMS added, invalidating email-only assumption from session 3). This tests decision persistence, assumption validation, cross-feature interference, and context recovery at realistic scale. Scores 5 dimensions including assumptionHandling which directly measures Twining's RECONSIDER mechanism.

alternatives.reason_rejected: Same feature, same task type — doesn't test heterogeneous work or requirement changes
Each micro-scenario starts fresh — doesn't test accumulated decision volume or cross-feature interference
